prompt: Why don’t we see the world blur when our eyes jump from point to point?

options.text: The brain briefly blocks visual processing during the jump
The eyes move too slowly to blur the image
The retina takes a photo before each movement

explanation: During saccades the retinal image blurs, but the brain selectively blocks visual processing.

prompt: How do we know the brain itself switches the suppression on?

options.text: It starts before the eye begins to move
It only happens in the dark
It only appears in short-sighted people

explanation: Because it starts before the saccade begins, it can’t be triggered by the moving image.
